claim: Conducted a 45-minute AEIOU contextual observation of a participant preparing a meal to map activities, tools, and workflow breakdowns.
detail: Logged timestamped interactions across 10 kitchen objects in a two-counter layout and identified breakdowns involving a missing towel and rinsed produce.

claim: Analyzed qualitative therapist interview data using CAQDAS coding and an Excel affinity diagram on game-based patient rehabilitation.
detail: Synthesized themes across physical, cognitive, and speech therapy workflows, documenting how clinicians tailor Wii Sports and iPad games by patient age.

claim: On a team of three, synthesized findings from 12 participants into design implications for integrated hybrid-work tools.
detail: Found disconnected-tool inefficiencies in all six participants and unstructured-meeting frustration in four of six, recommending cross-tool integration, automation, and flexible video options.

claim: On a team of three, conducted two weeks of interviews with six hybrid and remote professionals on scheduling and meeting engagement.
detail: Explored daily routines, communication habits, tool shortcomings, and ideal workflow solutions across task management, scheduling, and meetings.

claim: On a team of three, ran a three-week observation study with six hybrid and remote professionals on task and meeting workflows.
detail: Observed six professionals across two tasks: daily task management and meeting scheduling, and delivering information in a video scrum.

claim: On a team of three, developed personas and a persona spectrum from interview findings on hybrid-work workflows.
detail: Synthesized interview data from six professionals into user archetypes capturing task prioritization, scheduling, and meeting engagement patterns.

claim: On a team of three, reviewed Zoom fatigue literature and created a screener survey to recruit hybrid-work participants.
detail: Set eligibility criteria requiring three or more years of remote or hybrid work experience and use of Zoom, Microsoft Teams, or Slack.

claim: Ran 30–45 minute semi-structured interviews with six remote and hybrid professionals on a three-person team to investigate meeting overload and tool switching.
detail: Authored a screener and interview protocol covering daily routines, camera-off habits, task reprioritization, and AI note-taking across Zoom, Teams, and Slack.

claim: Conducted structured observations with six remote and hybrid professionals as part of a three-person team to study daily task scheduling and Zoom fatigue.
detail: Split 30-minute sessions equally between in-person and Zoom, having participants build a daily schedule and write a brief after a six-minute mock scrum call.

claim: Synthesized observation and interview data as part of a three-person team using affinity diagramming and a structured interview codebook.
detail: Identified three themes—meeting fatigue and engagement, task prioritization across disconnected tools, and scheduling optimization—across 12 total participants.

claim: Authored remote workday scenarios as part of a three-person team mapping cross-tool scheduling, focus-time blocking, and follow-up workflows.
detail: Documented end-to-end tool switching across Slack, Zoom, Google Calendar, Trello, Outlook Calendar, and Microsoft Teams for project and engineering workflows.

claim: Reviewed peer-reviewed studies on Zoom fatigue with a three-person team to frame cognitive load, non-verbal cue strain, and remote burnout.
detail: Synthesized five 2022–2024 publications linking prolonged videoconferencing and meeting overload to stress, reduced focus, and depressive symptoms.

claim: Co-authored a UX research report on a three-person team proposing integrated scheduling, AI meeting summaries, and interactive controls to curb Zoom fatigue.
detail: Recommended unifying calendar, chat, and task apps with manual time-blocking overrides, polls, whiteboards, and flexible camera-off modes for passive attendees.

claim: Conducted a competitive analysis of Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Slack on meeting-fatigue mitigation and async workflows.
detail: Evaluated AI summarization, notification controls, and SharePoint integrations, noting adoption barriers from extra licensing and hardware requirements.

claim: Authored a 30-45 minute semi-structured interview protocol studying task management and Zoom fatigue across six remote and hybrid professionals.
detail: Included screener criteria for Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Slack users, informed consent scripts, and questions on meeting load and tool gaps.

claim: Synthesized five academic and industry sources on remote-work fatigue, boundary control, and self-efficacy into a research report.
detail: Reviewed regression and path-analysis studies alongside a meta-analysis of 108 remote-work-intensity studies to frame research questions and recruitment.

claim: Evaluated four survey error sources and designed sampling and pilot-testing mitigations for a UX practitioner survey.
detail: Addressed coverage, nonresponse, sample size, and measurement errors using stratified sampling, multi-channel outreach, and interviewer standardization.

claim: Critiqued flawed survey items for precision, double-barreled wording, clarity, and double negatives, rewriting each with neutral options.
detail: Replaced vague frequency labels with quantifiable time intervals and split compound questions to reduce respondent confusion and bias.
